title: Localization of a ring at one element
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\varpi\in R$, and let $S=\{1,\varpi,\varpi^2,\dots\}$. The *localization of $R$ at $\varpi$* (*away from $\varpi$*) is the ring $R[1/\varpi]=R_\varpi=S^{-1}R$ of fractions $x/\varpi^n$ ($x\in R$, $n\geq0$), where $x/\varpi^n=y/\varpi^m$ if and only if $\varpi^k(x\varpi^m-y\varpi^n)=0$ for some $k\geq0$, with $x/s+y/t=(xt+ys)/st$ and $(x/s)(y/t)=xy/st$, together with the ring map $R\to R[1/\varpi]$, $x\mapsto x/1$, which makes $R[1/\varpi]$ an $R$-algebra in which $\varpi$ is invertible. More generally an $R$-algebra $A$ *is a localization of $R$ at $\varpi$* if the induced map $R[1/\varpi]\to A$ is an isomorphism; equivalently, the image of $\varpi$ in $A$ is a unit, every element of $A$ is $x\cdot\varpi^{-n}$, and $x\mapsto0$ in $A$ iff $\varpi^kx=0$ for some $k$.
